bug_semantics: fast-jwt createVerifier decoded the JWS header and then checked only alg/signature/claims. RFC 7515 section 4.1.11 requires that if header.crit lists any extension the recipient does not understand and support, the JWS is invalid. Through v6.1.0 src/verifier.js never inspected header.crit, so a token with crit:["x-custom-policy"] and a matching custom header was accepted after a valid HMAC/signature. That is CWE-345 / CWE-636 failing-open on unknown critical extensions (split-brain vs jose, policy/cnf bypass).
flaw_origin: The omission was present in the first implementation of src/verifier.js, commit 51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790 (feat(wip): Initial version, author/committer Shogun <shogun@cowtech.it>). That commit added verifyJwt as decode then verifyAlgorithm then verifySignature then verifyPayload with no crit handling. Parent 5063678a36ff118da9671f1f1df3d67cc95d1169 is scaffolding only (no src/). Later verifier rewrites kept the same gap until 80b49c73cf708701e1e3da7c16ef735789cb269c added validateCrit and allowedCritHeaders, released in v6.2.0.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: the sink is createVerifier accepting a JWS whose crit names an unsupported extension. That behavior is an omission in the original verifier, not a later feature. 51fe1ea3 is the smallest public first-write of src/verifier.js; the parent tree has no verifier; later refactors are carriers.
